variants.commentary: The apparatus prints φως 1°] pr το p. The article is an addition before the first occurrence of φῶς, not before its second occurrence. It may reflect grammatical smoothing or local textual history; this explanation remains a hypothesis. Hebrew אור lacks an article here, but that alone cannot decide the Greek reading. No dating or genealogical priority is inferred from the local siglum p.

readings.reading: επεφερετω
readings.evidence: Cambridge 1906 first apparatus, visually inspected; terminal omega as printed

variants.commentary: The first apparatus prints επεφερετω E against the reading text ἐπεφέρετο. The alternative is retained unaccented exactly as the apparatus gives it; no accentuation or morphological reinterpretation is silently supplied. The final-omega spelling belongs in an orthographic layer, not among automatically adopted substantive changes. The edition introduction identifies E as Codex Bodleianus, but a full witness/hand concordance and direct manuscript check remain outstanding. The baseline omicron spelling is retained provisionally. An initially considered U₂ entry is excluded: the special fragment/translation material requires separate identification before it can be treated as an ordinary LXX manuscript omission.

variants.commentary: The imported Greek has completion on the sixth day, as do the newly acquired Samaritan CB 751-based transcription (הששי) and ETCBC Peshitta (ܫܬܝܬܝܐ). OSHB and the selected Onkelos version have the seventh. All five give the seventh day for resting. This is a checked comparison of named digital sources, not a full collation of the Samaritan or Peshitta traditions or their printed apparatuses. An early Hebrew difference and an interpretive adjustment avoiding completion on the Sabbath remain competing explanations; agreement does not by itself establish independence. Megillah 9a:13 reports a sixth/seventh distinction as a translation change, but its later reception story is not a direct early Greek witness. The imported DSS 4Q10 completion ordinal is entirely reconstructed: source nodes 1941895 (ה) and 1941896 (שביעי) have zero nonreconstructed consonants. It must not be cited as preserved seventh-day support. No new OG reading is adopted.

readings.reading: ܘܐܡ̣ܪ ܩܐܝܢ ܠܗܒܝܠ ܐܚܘܗܝ. ܢܪܕܐ ܠܦܩܥܬܐ. ܘܗܘ̣ܐ ܕܟܕ ܗ̣ܢܘܢ ܒܚܩܠܐ . ܩܡ ܩܐܝܢ ܥܠ ܗܒܝܠ ܐܚܘܗܝ ܘܩܛܠܗ.

variants.commentary: The imported Greek includes διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πεδίον; the acquired Samaritan transcription has נלכה השדה, and the Peshitta has ܢܪܕܐ ܠܦܩܥܬܐ, both invitations to go to the field/plain. OSHB and this Onkelos version lack the quoted invitation. Loss in a Hebrew ancestor, explanatory expansion and cross-traditional influence remain competing accounts. These named sources do not establish the readings of all Samaritan or Syriac witnesses. The imported 4Q2 context has both reconstructed and uncertain letters around Abel and the following narrative clause; the transcription alone is insufficient for a new palaeographic judgement about space for the invitation. Accordingly no independent Qumran support for either length is assigned. The fuller Greek baseline is retained provisionally, without an OG-priority claim.

variants.commentary: The Greek source gives nine for Joseph’s Egyptian descendants and seventy-five for the household. OSHB, Onkelos, the acquired Samaritan transcription and the Peshitta give two and seventy. These are related genealogical totals and require study with Gen 46:20 and the whole list, not correction of an isolated numeral. No imported Genesis-labelled DSS units occur at Gen 46:27; this is a statement of this extraction’s coverage, not a claim about all Judaean Desert evidence or the separate Exodus tradition. Peshitta/Samaritan main-text agreement is now checked digitally, while their apparatuses and manuscript histories remain uncollated. No reading is adopted solely from majority agreement.
